decisions.reason: The referral-code metadata source does not change resale transfer semantics; the buyer's receipt of the mint-number referral code is separately and fully represented by the candidate's same-message INTRODUCE.
Defining the mint number as the referral-code metadata source does not change badge milestones, storage, approved designs, or current badge effects.
The FAQ's same-message INTRODUCE already states that the mint number is the permanent referral code and identifies its display locations, so no additional MODIFY is needed.
The candidate's same-message INTRODUCE already fully establishes each NFT's mint number as its permanent referral code.
The source decision identifies the referral-code attribute source but does not alter behavior when no referral code is used.
The commission amount, recipient, trigger, and automatic payout remain unchanged; identifying the referral code as the NFT mint number does not modify those payout rules.
The referral-code identity does not change the mint price or allocation amounts and destinations.
The metadata source for referral codes does not alter secondary-sale royalty amounts, visibility, allocation, or ticket-generation behavior.
The source decision does not change ticket issuance quantities, counters, eligibility windows, or post-draw reset behavior.
The referral-code metadata source does not change Big Block prize amounts, winner count, funding, or draw conditions.
The referral-code metadata source does not change Small Block prize amounts, funding sources, or draw conditions.
The referral-code metadata source is independent of the fiat provider, conversion path, supported payment methods, and wallet requirement.
